scope.note: Audited the frozen local commit (not yet pushed). Scope is every key whose English value changed in base..head in the nine namespaces, read with its context entry and the locale's old and new values; unchanged keys in these files were not re-audited for meaning. Whole-file mechanical checks (key-set parity with English, bidi control characters) cover all keys.

references.core_revision_note: origin/main of the local ~/local-operator clone as it stood at audit time (read with git show; not fetched during this audit).

method.read: Each changed key was read for meaning, idiom, register and term consistency against the English source, its context entry, the core glossary, the locale style guide and existing catalogue precedent at this head.
mechanical_checks_executed: key set of each target file equals the English key set
top-level ICU argument names and brace balance of every changed key equal the English ones
no manual bidi control characters (U+200E/F, U+202A-E, U+2066-9, U+061C) in any value of the nine target files

for keys whose only English change was 'Team plan' -> 'Radient Team plan', the target differs from its base value only by the inserted 'Radient ' (or is byte-identical where the locale already carried it)
no value in the locale's ui.* catalogues still names the plan without 'Radient'
method.not_done: No rendered frames, pseudo-localization, width/fit measurement or native-speaker review. No tests, builds or gates were run. This is a text audit only.

acceptance.plan_name: Consistent: 'plan Radient Team' in every audited key.
acceptance.credit_claim: ui.onboarding.connect.intro keeps all three conditions (eligible new accounts, email verification, security check), states no amount and uses 'can', so it makes no unconditional free-credit claim.
acceptance.no_free_usage_claim: ui.providers...one_browser_sign_in_nothing_to_paste says no subscription or API key is needed and does not say usage is free or unlimited.
acceptance.see_plan: ui.teamBridge.plan.see_plan is a neutral 'see/view', not buy/upgrade/subscribe.

findings.problem: 'un modelo en tu ordenador' uses the Spain-marked word 'ordenador'; the es style guide requires neutral Spanish that reads the same in Madrid and Mexico City, and the catalogue's own precedent is 'equipo' (ui.providers.connect_provider_card.use_a_model_on_this_computer = 'Usar un modelo en este equipo'). This is the only 'ordenador' in the es catalogues.
findings.suggested_fix: '... una clave de API o un modelo en este equipo.'

findings.problem: 'pasar un control de seguridad' reads like a physical checkpoint; a verification step is more naturally 'una comprobación de seguridad'. Meaning (conditional credit after email verification and a security check) is intact.
findings.suggested_fix: '... tras verificar su correo y superar una comprobación de seguridad.'
